simple.meaning: מְגַר (mᵉgar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to overthrow.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 1 time across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 6:12. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְגַר (H4049).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מְגַר (mᵉgar) / H4049 is traced through Ezra 6:12 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and peoples who stretch out their hand to alter this, to destroy this house of God which is at Jerusalem. I Darius have made a decree. Let it be done with all diligence.

definitions.full: H4049. megar [ מְגַר ] verb Pa`el overthrow ( ᵑ7 , Syriac (Lexicons); see Biblical Hebrew (late, rare)); — Imperfect 3masculine singular כָּלמֶֿלֶךְ יְמַגַּר Ezra 6:12 (of God). [ מַדְבַּח ] see דבח . מִדָּה see ׳מִנ . [ מְדוֺר ] see דור .
